subtype: Approach: avoiding reminders and refusing to talk [Pitfall]
passage: I'm Yusuf. After Nani died in March, I put every photo of her in a drawer, even the one on the fridge, because seeing her face felt like a slap. When Amma started a sentence with “Remember when Nani...”, I got up and left the room. Jahnavi, my little sister, would say, “Bhaiya, please stay,” and I would close my door. I thought if I didn't look, it would stop hurting. It didn't. It sat there, sharper, and came out at strange moments, like when I smelled her cardamom tea in a shop. Meanwhile dinner grew quiet. Amma and Jahnavi shared stories without me, and I felt a wall growing between us. Looking back, running away made the pain last longer and made me lonelier.

qa.q: What did Yusuf do with every photo of Nani?
qa.a: Yusuf put every photo of her in a drawer.

qa.q: What was Yusuf feeling when he saw Nani's face?
qa.a: Yusuf felt deeply hurt, since seeing her face felt like a slap, so he hid the photos.
Yusuf could stay for one short story and let the sadness come, maybe with a photo in view, since sharing memories can soften the pain over time.

qa.q: How might Jahnavi feel when Yusuf leaves the room?
qa.a: Jahnavi probably feels sad and shut out, since she asks Bhaiya to stay and he closes his door.

grounding: A teen puts away every photo and leaves the room when the person is mentioned, hoping the pain will vanish, but avoidance keeps it sharp and distances him from family.

subtype: Approach: avoiding reminders and refusing to talk [Pitfall]
passage:
Housemaster's note, Sunday.
Tenzin's mother and uncle visited today, three weeks after his Mola's death. They brought a small album and a khata she had kept. The moment his mother opened the album in the visitors' room, Tenzin stood up, said he had football, and left. His mother sat holding the book, looking hurt.
This fits what I've seen. He took Mola's framed photo off his locker the day after the news. When boys in his dorm mention her, he walks out. He sleeps badly and snaps at small things. Avoiding every reminder isn't dulling the pain; it seems to keep it raw, and keeps his family outside it.
Next steps: I spoke with his mother before she left. I'll ask the school counsellor to see him this week, and she'll phone him on Wednesday, just to talk, no album.
Kishore Sir

qa.q: What did Tenzin's family bring on the visit?
qa.a: They brought a small album and a khata Mola had kept.

qa.q: What might Tenzin have been feeling when he left the visitors' room?
qa.a: Tenzin was likely overwhelmed by grief and afraid of feeling it, so leaving felt safer than looking at the album.

qa.q: What else could help Tenzin besides the counsellor?
qa.a: His family could offer small, gentle chances to remember Mola, like one photo or one story, instead of a whole album at once.

qa.q: How is Tenzin's mother affected by his leaving?
qa.a: His mother is left holding the album, hurt, because she wanted to grieve together and he shut her out.

grounding: Shows a teen hiding every photo and leaving whenever his grandmother is mentioned, which keeps the pain sharp and pushes away family who want to share it.

passage:
Thursday night
Vidya put Appa's photo back on the shelf again today. I had moved it into the cupboard on Monday, with his watch and the old cricket cap. I can't walk past his face every time I get water.
At dinner Amma said, "Appa would have liked this rasam," and I got up and went to my room. Vidya followed and stood in the doorway. "You always leave. We want to talk about him. You act like he never existed." I told her to get out.
It's been two months. I thought if I didn't look or listen, it would fade. It doesn't. Tonight I heard Amma and Vidya laughing in the kitchen about his terrible jokes, and it hurt worse than anything, because I wasn't in there with them.
Shankar

qa.q: Where had Shankar put Appa's photo on Monday?
qa.a: Shankar had moved it into the cupboard.

qa.q: What did Shankar feel on hearing Amma and Vidya laughing?
qa.a: Shankar felt hurt and left out, because avoiding every reminder had kept the pain sharp and put distance from the family.

qa.q: What would you change first for Shankar?
qa.a: Shankar could try staying for one small memory at dinner, or tell Vidya it's hard and ask to go slowly, instead of leaving every time.

qa.q: How does Vidya experience Shankar walking out?
qa.a: Vidya feels shut out and angry, because she wants to talk about Appa together and Shankar keeps leaving.

grounding: Illustrates a teen putting away every photo and leaving when a dead parent is mentioned, and finding that avoidance keeps the pain sharp and shuts out the family.
